chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shuayb who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays upon his riding animal. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He indicates by gestures, making the prostration lower than the bowing.' I said, 'Can he pray while he is walking?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, indicating by gestures, and let him make the prostration lower than the bowing.'
ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim perform prayer gestures while riding an animal during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanics of 'salat al-musafir' (prayer during travel), establishing that when riding a beast, the rider performs prayer through head gestures (iima') rather than full physical postures. It specifically mandates that the prostration gesture be lower than the bowing gesture, a ruling that applies whether the rider is stationary or moving, reflecting the practical flexibility (rukhas) granted in Shia jurisprudence for travelers.
